title: mapant pipeline parameters
description: Generate a web-mercator vector map (PMTiles) from a list of LiDAR tiles using karttapullautin.

tiles_csv.description: CSV listing the LiDAR tiles to process.
tiles_csv.help_text: One row per .laz/.las file with its URL, size, sha256, CRS and projected bounding box. This file is the pipeline's input contract; see assets/schema_tiles.json for the full column list. Any region or country can be processed by producing a CSV that satisfies it.

osm_pbf.description: OpenStreetMap extract used to draw roads, buildings and water.
osm_pbf.help_text: Optional. Without it the map has contours, cliffs and vegetation only. A single country-sized .pbf is fine: the pipeline cuts a per-grid extract from it, and each grid's renderer is handed only its own.

pullauta_ini.description: karttapullautin parameter file controlling the cartography.
pullauta_ini.help_text: Everything about the map's appearance -- contour interval, the vegetation and cliff models, form lines. The pipeline overrides only the keys it must own (batch mode, thread count, input/output folders) and publishes the result as the run's provenance record.

vectorconf.description: Shape mapping file (osm.txt) translating OSM tags to ISOM map symbols.

outdir.description: Where the map archive, its viewer, QC files and provenance are written.

publish_mode.description: How published files leave the work directory.
publish_mode.help_text: 'copy' works everywhere including object stores. 'link' (hardlink) avoids copying the country-sized archive, but needs outdir and workDir on one filesystem. Never use 'move': it breaks -resume.

map_title.description: Title of the map, shown in the viewer and written into the archive's metadata.

attribution.description: Credit for the LiDAR data, shown on the map next to OpenStreetMap and karttapullautin.
attribution.help_text: HTML is allowed, e.g. 'Bayerische Vermessungsverwaltung'. Most open LiDAR licences require it.

region.title: Region filter
region.description: Restrict the run to part of the tiles CSV. The halo is always drawn from the whole CSV, so a filtered region renders identically to a full run.

region_bbox.description: Only render tiles intersecting this box: 'minx,miny,maxx,maxy'.

region_bbox_crs.description: CRS of region_bbox: 'lonlat', or an EPSG string meaning the tiles' own CRS.

grid_size.description: Tiles per grid edge; a download/disk trade-off.
grid_size.help_text: Each grid is rendered with one ring of neighbouring tiles around it, which is what karttapullautin's 127 m halo needs. Larger grids re-fetch proportionally fewer ring tiles (2.8x at 3, 1.44x at 10, 1.27x at 16) but need proportionally more disk per concurrent task -- roughly (grid_size+2)^2 tiles plus karttapullautin's temporaries.

pullauta_processes.description: karttapullautin worker threads per grid; also the task's cpus.
pullauta_processes.help_text: Each worker needs roughly 2 GB of RAM and about 3 GB of scratch for its own temporary files.

max_pullauta_attempts.description: How many times to re-run a grid while isolating tiles that crash the renderer.
max_pullauta_attempts.help_text: A karttapullautin panic aborts the whole process, so the grid is re-run -- it resumes by itself, skipping finished tiles. An attempt that makes no progress is retried single-threaded, which identifies the offending tile unambiguously; that tile is then recorded in qc/pullauta_failures.tsv and skipped, while still serving as a neighbour for the tiles around it.

download_jobs.help_text: Multiplied by the number of concurrent grids and by the number of nodes, this is how hard the pipeline hits the data provider. Open-data servers are usually not built for it; keep it modest and consider download_limit_rate.

download_retries.description: Attempts per file before the grid is failed for retry.

osm_chunk_size.description: Grids per osmium pass over the source .pbf.
osm_chunk_size.help_text: One pass reads the whole .pbf, so batching many extracts into it avoids re-reading a country per grid. The ceiling is memory: --strategy=smart holds a set of object ids per extract.

osm_buffer_m.description: Buffer added around each grid before cutting its OSM extract.
osm_buffer_m.help_text: Together with the extract strategy, this is what keeps objects that straddle a grid boundary intact.

osm_strategy.help_text: 'smart' keeps ways and multipolygon relations whole, so a lake or road crossing the boundary still renders as one object. 'simple' is faster but cuts them.

base_zoom.description: Shallowest zoom level of the pyramid, and the unit tiling is parallelised over.
base_zoom.help_text: One task per base-zoom tile, cutting everything under it: a tile one zoom shallower covers four times the ground and needs about four times the memory. Raise it on a memory-constrained machine. Nothing is generated below it -- the viewer shows OSM's own tiles there instead.

max_zoom.help_text: The zoom the map is cut at full detail, in 512 px tiles (MapLibre's convention); the layer table in make_vector_tiles.py brings detail in counting down from it (e.g. undergrowth from max_zoom-2). Vector tiles stay sharp when the viewer overzooms them, so z15 -- as much detail per screen pixel as z16 in 256 px tiles -- is enough for the full LiDAR detail. Each extra level roughly quadruples the archive.
